info.desc: Rocket to Russia is the third studio album by the American punk rock band Ramones. It was released on November 4, 1977 through Sire Records. It was their last with original drummer Tommy Ramone. The album incorporates surf rock and other influences. It includes some of the Ramones' best-known songs, including "Sheena Is a Punk Rocker" and "Teenage Lobotomy". In 2003, the album was ranked number 105 on Rolling Stone magazine's list of The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time. .

podcast.body: Released in 1977, this album is considered one of the most influential punk rock records of all time. It contains pervasive surf influences, evident in songs like "Rockaway Beach," "Do You Wanna Dance," and "Sheena Is A Punk Rocker," showcasing the band's appreciation for 60s surf rock. "Their third album, 1977's Rocket to Russia, one of the most influential punk rock records of all time, has surf influences all over the place, whether it's a song like Rock Away Beach, or do you want to dance, or even Shina is a punk rocker."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released on November 4th, 1977, just 11 months after *Ramones Leave Home*, completing a streak of three albums in 18 months. Tommy Ramone co-produced this album as well. Its release coincided with the peak of punk rock, making it a "seriously important record" for the time. Johnny Ramone was highly motivated by the Sex Pistols' "God Save the Queen," feeling they had "ripped off the Ramone sound." The album features iconic songs that would forever be staples in the Ramones' setlist, including "Rockaway Beach," "Sheena Is a Punk Rocker," and "Cretin Hop (We're a Happy Family)." This album marked Tommy Ramone's last as the band's drummer. "A fine record, but it would be the last with drummer Tommy Ramone."
